subject: Transition kickoff — model slate, context length, and token forecast
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@skyward.ai>, Skyward Onboarding <onboarding@skyward.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Transition kickoff — model slate, context length, and token forecast

Hi Ethan / Skyward team,

Great to meet you on the demo yesterday — thanks for the time. This thread is to capture the initial handoff from Sales -> CS/Implementation so we can lock the model shortlist and sizing assumptions before engineering kicks off. I've attached a basic token_profile.csv with the sample payloads you shared; please confirm or replace with anything more representative.

To keep momentum, can you confirm the following by EOD Monday:
- Primary product flows we’ll support first (search-assist, summarization, question-answering)
- Typical and peak prompt length (characters/words) and expected average response size in tokens
- Expected concurrent users (or API QPS) during peak and typical windows
- Any hard latency SLOs (p90/p99) or cost guardrails for the pilot

Initial ask from our side: we plan to evaluate three model tiers for the pilot (conservative, balanced, high-capacity) and run short A/B evals using your sample prompts. Suggested next steps from Redwood:
- Redwood runs evals on 3 candidate variants and returns latency/cost/quality matrix (2 business days)
- Align on a canary rollout plan (traffic %, rollout windows)
- Finalize Mutual Action Plan and contract milestone for Dedicated capacity if chosen

Attachments: token_profile.csv (sample tokenization of your representative prompts)

I'll schedule a 30 min kickoff next week to walk through the questions and the timeline; please propose times that work.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

---

Note: internal recipients (Grace, Monica) — once Ethan confirms the usage numbers we should pick model candidates for evaluation. My initial thinking below is conservative: 13B quantized candidate, 30B float-lite candidate, and a baseline 7B fast candidate for cost comparison.
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@skyward.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyward Onboarding <onboarding@skyward.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transition kickoff — model slate, context length, and token forecast

Vanessa — thanks, attaching our usage snapshot and a short sample set (see usage_snapshot.csv). Quick answers inline:

- Primary flows: 70% search-assist (short prompts, multi-turn), 20% document summarization (longer context), 10% proactive insights (mixed)
- Typical prompt length: 40–120 tokens; average response: 30–100 tokens
- Summarization flow: up to 12k characters; estimated 3–4k token window for the biggest documents (we can pre-chunk but want a model that handles at least 4k tokens comfortably)
- Peak concurrency: anticipated pilot peak ~120 concurrent API connections; expected peak QPS ~45 (bursty by minute)
- Latency: p90 <= 800ms is ideal for search-assist; p99 <= 2s preferable but not a blocker initially
- Cost guardrail: pilot monthly token spend target $15k–$25k

Attachments: usage_snapshot.csv, examples_sample.json

We can do the kickoff call Mon/Tue mornings PT. Let me know what you need from our side for the evals.

—Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Product, Skyward Analytics
ethan.cole@skyward.ai
+1 206-555-2424

Subject: Internal: Skyward pilot — shortlist + sizing recommendation

Grace / Monica — forwarding Ethan's reply and usage snapshot. Key takeaways: 4k token context required for summarization path, pilot peak ~45 QPS (bursty), target p90 800ms, pilot token budget $15k–$25k/mo.

Proposed evaluation plan (48–72 hours of work):
- Candidate A (cost-first): 7B distilled chat model (q4_0 quantized) — target p90 ~300–600ms for short prompts, best cost per token.
- Candidate B (balanced): 13B quantized conversational model (q4_0/q4_K) — handles multi-turn better, should meet p90 ~600–900ms with smart batching and prefix cache.
- Candidate C (capacity/quality): 30B hybrid (int8/float mix) — intended for summarization/long-context where coherence matters; expect higher cost, p90 ~900–1400ms.

Operational notes:
- For the 4k summarization window we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching and chunked inference with stitched outputs for large docs; that should reduce effective latency for repeated queries.
- Autoscale plan: reserve a small baseline Dedicated pool for pilot (2 GPUs of balanced class) with burst to hosted capacity on spikes; this keeps cost predictable and falls within their pilot budget when combined with quantized candidates.
- Eval matrix: quality (ROUGE/BERTScore on sample set), p90/p99 latency, cost per 1M tokens, failure rate under bursty request pattern.

Action items:
- Monica: can you spin the eval runs on Candidate A/B/C using Ethan's samples (examples_sample.json) and return the matrix + short notes? Aim: 48–72 hours.
- Grace: I'll loop in Solutions Eng for the prefix cache config and canary plan; please prepare a short playbook for the rollout steps and rollback criteria.

I’ll coordinate the kickoff call with Ethan for Monday AM PT; if either of you see a blocker call it out now.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
